name: type-safe-enum
intent: Give a fixed set of constants its own nominal type whose legal values are exactly the declared members, so values cannot be mixed with - or silently converted from - unrelated integers and strings.
problem: A fixed set of related constants is represented as bare integers or strings (`public static final int APPLE_FUJI = 0`, `#define SEASON_SPRING "spring"`): nothing stops a caller from passing an unrelated number, adding two members, comparing across two different sets, or mistyping a string; the compiler cannot distinguish a typo from a valid value and the mistake surfaces at run time.
context: Whenever a domain concept is a mutually exclusive, compile-time-known set of alternatives - order states, card suits, log levels, protocol codes - and those values travel through method signatures, persistence and wire formats where the underlying primitive (int, ordinal, string) is also used for unrelated purposes. It matters most where an invalid value must fail compilation rather than corrupt data, and where the set is declared once and used by many callers.
benefits: Compile-time closure: the type admits only the declared members, so an unrelated integer, a mistyped string or another set's value is rejected by the compiler (or the type checker) instead of being accepted as data.
Each set gets its own namespace: identically named constants coexist in different sets and the prefix convention (SUIT_, SEASON_) that int enums require disappears.
Name, value and behaviour live in one declaration: members carry fields, labels and methods, so knowledge about the set sits with the set instead of in scattered switch statements.

Insulation between the set and its clients: callers reference named members, so members can be added or reordered without recompiling callers as long as ordinals are not persisted (enum types are designed for binary-compatible evolution).
A single conversion point: external representations are parsed, validated and formatted in one place, which is exactly where unknown or legacy values are handled.
Tool support: exhaustive match/switch checking, iteration over members and enum-keyed collections (EnumSet/EnumMap, entries, allCases) instead of hand-maintained arrays and count constants.
tradeoffs: Closed by design: adding a member is a source change that breaks every exhaustive match and switch, so third-party or data-driven extension is out of scope - that is Type Object's or an extension interface's job.

Boundary mapping becomes explicit work: persistence, transport and interop each need a conversion, and choosing the wrong representation (ordinal versus name versus custom key) turns into a silent data bug.
Ordinal coupling: runtimes expose ordinal()/declaration order and invite callers to persist it; reordering or inserting members then changes stored meaning.

Ceremony for small sets: a full type - sometimes a class hierarchy or generated converters - where a single constant sufficed, and some realizations drag runtime baggage (TypeScript enum objects, Java class files per enum).

Serializers, ORMs and schema tools often do not understand the enum type out of the box, so frameworks need custom converters or type registrations and the primitive has to be exposed at the edges, where it can be abused.
Where the language lacks the construct (C, JavaScript) the realization only approximates it: discipline, warning flags and runtime validation replace the compiler guarantee.

participants.responsibility: Nominal type that owns the closed set and its namespace; construction is private so no instance can be created outside it.
One immutable singleton instance standing for one alternative; carries the member name and any data or behaviour attached to it.
Parse/format/validate functions translating between external representations (integer, ordinal, text key) and members, rejecting unknown values.

use_cases: Domain vocabularies with a fixed set of alternatives: order and payment states, card suits, log levels, HTTP methods, units of measure.
Replacing legacy int or string constants (int enum pattern, #define groups, static final String) so that invalid or mistyped values stop compiling.
Values that cross a persistence or transport boundary, where one conversion and validation point is wanted for parsing and formatting.
Enum-keyed collections and configuration (EnumSet/EnumMap, entries, allCases, switch exhaustiveness) instead of parallel arrays and count constants.
A small closed family of algorithms or policies whose members carry their own data and behaviour (constant-specific methods, strategy enums).
State machines and protocols in which a value must be one of a fixed, compiler-known set and illegal states must be unrepresentable.

The JDK's java.time API models month-of-year and day-of-week as the enum types Month and DayOfWeek, which carry explicit getValue() integers aligned with ISO-8601 and behavior like plus()/maxLength(), so calendar APIs (LocalDate.of(year, Month, dayOfMonth)) accept members, never bare ints; the Javadoc tells callers to prefer getValue() over ordinal().

Protocol Buffers compiles each .proto enum into a closed enum type in the generated target-language code (Java, C++, C#, Python EnumDescriptor), and the wire boundary converts via forNumber() with proto3's UNRECOGNIZED member or integer retention, exemplifying the single validated conversion point for a cross-language vocabulary.

Django ships models.TextChoices and models.IntegerChoices (built on Python's enum.Enum) as the typed way to declare model field choices: the field takes the enum class, members carry value plus human-readable label, and .choices/.labels/.values drive validation and form rendering.
avoid_when: The set is open: plugins or configuration data add members at run time - use Type Object, a registry, or an extensible enum with a common interface.
Members carry heterogeneous payloads and are matched structurally - use an algebraic data type / sealed hierarchy / tagged union (Option, Either) instead.
The choice is genuinely binary and local to one function - a plain boolean, or no constant at all, is simpler.
The values are only a wire or database encoding of a richer open concept (ISO currency codes, country codes, MIME types) and must stay data - model a value object plus a registry instead.
You only need combinable bit flags and the language has no Flag/EnumSet type - hand-rolled bitmasks recreate the int enum anti-pattern.
anti_patterns: Int enum pattern: a group of public static final int constants (or a #define group) used as an enum, so any int is accepted and arithmetic on members compiles.
String enum pattern: raw string constants for a closed set, so typos escape the compiler and comparisons depend on string equality rules.
Ordinal persistence: storing ordinal()/declaration position or relying on implicit numeric values, so inserting or reordering a member silently changes stored data.
Conversion abuse: casting arbitrary integers or strings into the enum type in many places instead of validating once at a boundary.
Repeating switch statements over the enum at many call sites instead of giving the members (or the type) the behaviour once.
design_principles: Type safety / make illegal states unrepresentable: the legal value set is part of the type, not a convention.
Avoid primitive obsession: a domain concept gets a named type instead of an int or string.
Single source of truth: members, their names and their associated behaviour are declared together.
Instance control and immutability: construction is private and members are immutable singletons.
Fail fast at the boundary: external representations are validated before they become enum values.
best_practices: Convert at the edges only: parse and validate external integers/strings exactly once, and never assign raw primitives to the enum type inside the domain.
Persist stable text keys or explicitly assigned values - never ordinals or implicit declaration order.
Keep matches exhaustive: omit default in statement switches so a new member fails the build, and end union/literal-type rewrites with a never-check.
Let members carry data and behaviour (constant-specific methods, strategy enums) instead of repeating switch logic at call sites.
Pin explicit values for any member set that crosses a wire, database or ABI boundary, and version the boundary instead of extending the enum.
Use the language's enum-keyed helpers (EnumSet/EnumMap, entries, CaseIterable) instead of arrays indexed by ordinal.
sources: Joshua Bloch, Effective Java (1st ed., 2001) - Item 21, the Typesafe Enum pattern; superseded by enum types in Effective Java 2nd/3rd ed., Item 34 'Use enums instead of int constants'.
